correctness.rationale: Henson universality and homogeneity give precisely all finite triangle-free adjacency diagrams. Thus admissible one-point neighborhoods are independent sets and ordered two-point diagrams split into I(1)^2 nonadjacent and Phi(G) adjacent cases. Both five-vertex examples have independence polynomial 1+5z+6z^2+2z^3 but Phi=105,103. Both connected six-vertex witnesses have polynomial 1+6z+9z^2+3z^3, equal degree multiset, nonisomorphic cycles, and Phi=209,203. The finite minimality and uniqueness claims follow from exhaustive 2^{10}-graph enumeration through order five, triangle-free filtering and all n! isomorphism relabellings; 14 order-five classes, one polynomial collision, no connected collision through five. The standalone verifier was run against the actual candidate source path and passed.

value.rationale: Complete one-point neighborhood-size spectra are intrinsic orbit invariants of the pointwise stabilizer in the classical homogeneous triangle-free graph. The theorem shows that these spectrally identical bases can nevertheless have distinct ordered two-type orbit counts and determines the first exact size at which this occurs. The connected six-point boundary, preserved degree sequence, and cycle-shape difference demonstrate that the failure is not only an isolated-point artifact. It is a naturally motivated finite cutoff, supported by a complete census at the first collision and concrete checks, not an arbitrary graph slice, generic complexity claim, or known-table recomputation alone.
